papers.title: A half-center oscillator regulates sleep pressure.
papers.summary: Using Drosophila dorsal fan-shaped body neurons, the study shows that sleep-control neurons generate slow-wave activity causally linked to sleep. The oscillations arise from bistable membrane potentials via interhemispheric competition between two half-centers connected by inhibitory glutamatergic synapses; disrupting glutamate release disrupts SWA and sleep, while optogenetic replay of SWA induces sleep.

papers.title: Neural Computation Runs on Dissipative Structures Under Cyclic Calibration: A Systems Perspective on Sleep
papers.summary: Proposes that sleep is a systemic recalibration phase for neural computation operating under thermodynamic constraints, counterbalancing entropic drift to maintain signaling parameters such as gain, threshold, and integration time. Reframes sleep need as an emergent property of dissipative neural computation rather than homeostatic regulation of unknown physiological variables.

papers.title: Progressive neurodegeneration of the locus coeruleus drives rapid eye movement sleep fragmentation
papers.summary: Used progressive Caspase-3-mediated locus coeruleus ablation in DBH-Cre mice with longitudinal sleep and calcium fiber photometry to test causal effects of LC degeneration on sleep. Found that REM sleep fragmentation emerged at mild degeneration (~25% loss), and at moderate degeneration (~50% loss) total REM sleep increased while REM EEG theta power declined and state-dependent LC calcium activity was blunted.

papers.title: Recovery sleep induces analgesia via sleep ensembles of the zona incerta acting through distinct neural circuits in mice.
papers.summary: The study identifies sleep-activated neuronal ensembles in the mouse zona incerta that mediate both NREM sleep and analgesia. Activating these ensembles increased NREM sleep and reduced pain sensitivity, while inhibition reversed these effects; neurotensin was enriched in these neurons, and separate projections to lateral hypothalamus and posterior thalamic nucleus selectively regulated sleep and analgesia, respectively.

papers.title: Disease progression shapes circadian and locomotor disruption in a model of multiple sclerosis
papers.summary: Characterized home-cage activity changes over the course of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) and tested whether continuous monitoring can serve as an observer-independent measure of disease progression. Mid-active/dark-phase locomotor activity was most affected; circadian disruption occurred at onset and peak, and >40-minute activity bouts detected non-motor symptoms independently of clinical motor scores.

papers.title: Between patterns and predictions: Interpretable latent EEG representations for clinical insights.
papers.summary: Applied a pretrained Universal Map of EEG latent embedding, without retraining, to three independent clinical EEG cohorts (cardiac arrest n=575, subarachnoid hemorrhage n=100, routine clinical n=141). Trajectory-derived geometric and temporal embedding features discriminated outcome in cardiac arrest (ROC-AUC 0.83) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (0.76) and distinguished physiological from pathological routine EEGs (0.93).

papers.title: Recombinant bovine αs1-casein ameliorates PCPA-induced insomnia-like behavioral and physiological abnormalities in mice.
papers.summary: Evaluated recombinant bovine αs1-casein (RC) in a PCPA-induced mouse model of insomnia and assessed behavior, neurotransmitters, cytokines, hippocampal histology, and cecal microbiota. RC improved body-weight recovery and open-field performance, increased brain 5-HT, 5-HIAA, dopamine, GABA, and glutamate, reduced elevated norepinephrine, lowered IL-6 at high dose, and was associated with altered bacterial richness and community structure.

papers.title: Modulating Sleep Oscillations Through Targeted Memory Reactivation: Linking Functional Dynamics to Brain Microstructure
papers.summary: In a study combining targeted memory reactivation (TMR) during sleep with high-density EEG and diffusion MRI, TMR decreased spindle density, slow oscillation density, and their co-occurrence compared to regular sleep; higher spindle density and co-occurrence were associated with greater overnight performance gains, and oscillatory measures correlated with learning-related microstructural changes in striatum and thalamus. Under the present stimulation conditions, TMR did not enhance motor memory consolidation but instead reduced sleep oscillatory activity and attenuated spindle-related connectivity dynamics.

papers.title: Slow Frontal Spindle Activity and Declarative Memory Retention During Daytime Naps.
papers.summary: In a daytime nap study with an object-location declarative memory task, nappers showed significantly better delayed memory retention than non-nappers. Within the nap group, memory was positively associated with local spindle density at frontal and parietal sites and with the proportion of slow frontal spindles clustered in trains during NREM2, though these associations did not reach significance under two-tailed testing.

papers.title: Vigilance profiles at sleep onset in patients with difficulty initiating sleep, with and without depressive or anxiety symptoms
papers.summary: Retrospective analysis of polysomnography from 2,952 sleep-clinic patients found that those with difficulty initiating sleep (DIS) had longer sleep latency and slightly higher vigilance markers during wakefulness and sleep, with only marginal differences in the sleep-onset period duration. Among unmedicated DIS patients, depressive symptoms were associated with a less wake-like sleep-onset period despite more severe insomnia complaints, suggesting that continuous EEG vigilance markers can help characterize insomnia heterogeneity.

papers.title: Frontal theta power prospectively associated with response inhibition.
papers.summary: Tested whether frontal-midline theta power measured with EEG before stop-signal trials reflects proactive response inhibition in healthy individuals across two experiments. FM theta was higher before successful stopping than failed stopping, but was also stronger before slow versus fast go trials, and FM alpha was specifically associated with proactive inhibition rather than slowing.

papers.title: Sleep EEG oscillations and synaptic plasticity in memory consolidation across NREM and REM sleep.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on how NREM and REM sleep oscillations interact with synaptic plasticity to support memory consolidation, describing mechanisms such as cortical slow oscillations, thalamic spindles, hippocampal sharp-wave ripples, synaptic downscaling, theta oscillations, and PGO waves. It identifies remaining challenges in cross-frequency coupling, glial contributions, and clinical translation.

papers.title: Circadian system and human health: From molecular mechanisms to clinical integration.
papers.summary: Reviews evidence that organ-specific physiological programs are governed by the circadian clock and that chronic circadian desynchronization contributes to multisystem disorders including neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, metabolic, and oncogenic pathologies. It assesses therapeutic modalities and proposes public health and behavioral interventions toward precision chronomedicine.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Selectively Alters Cellular Stress Responses During Exercise in the Heat in Young and Older Males.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
papers.summary: Examined whether 24-hour total sleep deprivation alters autophagy and cellular stress responses during exercise-heat stress in young and older males. Sleep deprivation did not broadly alter macroautophagy markers, but selectively modified chaperone-mediated autophagy and stress/apoptotic/inflammatory proteins, with older males showing reduced HSP90 and increased cleaved-caspase-3 and TNF-α.

papers.title: Abnormal resting-state EEG microstates correlate with objective sleep parameters in insomnia disorder.
papers.summary: This study compared resting-state EEG microstates in 45 insomnia disorder patients and 48 healthy controls and correlated microstate parameters with overnight polysomnography in a subset. Insomnia patients showed shorter microstates A and B, higher occurrence and contribution of microstate C, and reduced duration, occurrence, and contribution of microstate D, with microstate D occurrence negatively correlated with REM sleep proportion and positively correlated with N1 sleep proportion.

papers.title: Tracking Vigilance While Driving: Pilot Study of Heart Rate Variability Classification Under a Controlled Sleep-Deprivation Protocol.
papers.summary: This pilot study combined a 30-hour sleep-deprivation protocol, driving simulations every two hours, and machine-learning analysis of heart rate variability to classify vigilance states in 12 healthy young adults. HRV features differed between Rested and Tired states, and participant-independent classifiers achieved average accuracy greater than 85% in discriminating the two states.

papers.title: Clockophagy in Alzheimer's Disease: An Emerging Hypothesis Linking Circadian Dysfunction to Ferroptotic Vulnerability.
papers.summary: This review proposes clockophagy, an SQSTM1/p62-mediated selective autophagy process involved in BMAL1 degradation, as an emerging hypothesis linking circadian dysfunction to ferroptotic vulnerability in Alzheimer's disease. It summarizes evidence connecting sleep disruption, circadian dysfunction, lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis while highlighting limitations of current mechanistic evidence and potential therapeutic implications.

papers.title: An Efficient Convolutional Neural Network Model for Classifying Positive Affective States from EEG Data Considering Sleep Condition.
papers.summary: Developed a two-stage EEG framework that first classifies Normal Sleep versus Sleep-Deprived (CNN-BiLSTM) and then uses lightweight CNNs to recognize four affective states. Window-level accuracy reached 95.96% for the sleep stage and 93.40% (NS) and 90.95% (SD) for affect classification, whereas subject-independent cross-validation accuracy was only ~39%, highlighting cross-subject generalization limits.

papers.title: Automation in sleep state classification and maturity evaluation of EEG in preterm-born infants.
papers.summary: The study developed a deep learning model using a fine-tuned ResNet-50 to classify 30-second EEG segments from preterm-born infants into eight classes for noise detection, sleep state classification, and maturity assessment. The model achieved a macro F1 score of 0.58 for 8-class classification and 0.84 for merged active sleep, quiet sleep, and noise categories, and a novel maturity rate increased continuously with postmenstrual age.

papers.title: Is cardiovascular autonomic control during the day-to-night transition dependent on dim light melatonin onset? An exploratory analysis in healthy adults.
papers.summary: Exploratory study in 10 healthy adults using an ultra-short semi-constant routine tested whether dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) aligns with the day-to-night transition in cardiovascular autonomic control. Cardiovascular onset times did not differ significantly from DLMO, but DLMO–CV onset differences correlated strongly with phase angle of entrainment (r > 0.75), suggesting alignment depends on entrainment phase.

papers.title: Salivary Dim-Light Melatonin Onset is Associated with Functional Decline, Respiratory Symptom Emergence, and Survival in Early Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
papers.summary: This prospective longitudinal study assessed salivary dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) in 50 people with early amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and found that they had an earlier DLMO than controls. Within the ALS cohort, a later baseline DLMO was associated with worse functional status, faster disease progression, incident respiratory symptoms, and poorer survival/tracheostomy-free outcome.

papers.title: Neuroelectrophysiological correlates of extended cessation of consciousness in advanced meditators: A multimodal EEG and MEG study
papers.summary: First electrophysiological study of 'extended cessation' meditation, with five advanced meditators undergoing concurrent EEG and MEG. Extended cessation significantly increased high-frequency global coherence in all five participants without consistent effects on Lempel-Ziv complexity or power, suggesting a neural signature distinct from deep sleep and anesthesia.

papers.title: Scalp EEG and Intrinsic Optical Signal Imaging for Noninvasive Detection of Spreading Depolarizations in the Rat Cortex.
papers.summary: Using scalp EEG and intrinsic optical signal (IOS) recordings in rats, the study tested noninvasive detection of high-potassium-induced spreading depolarizations (SDs). Scalp EEG detected SD-related depression of AC-EEG activity but not DC-shifts, while concurrent infrared IOS captured reliable SD-associated signals; both techniques enabled high-fidelity SD detection despite smaller magnitudes than epidural recordings.

papers.title: Cannabinoids and sleep bruxism: mechanistic rationale, polysomnographic evidence, and future research directions.
papers.summary: This narrative review examined the relationship between cannabinoids (CBD, THC, CBN) and sleep bruxism (SB), synthesizing mechanistic and clinical evidence. It found that direct clinical evidence is limited, with one randomized trial showing topical CBD reduced a bruxism index, but no study has measured rhythmic masticatory muscle activity by polysomnography under any cannabinoid.

papers.title: Video EEG in pediatric epilepsy: Diagnostic significance and association between frequency band power and cognitive impairment severity.
papers.summary: The study compared video EEG (VEEG) and routine EEG for diagnosing epilepsy in 160 children and analyzed correlations between EEG frequency band power and cognitive impairment severity in 80 diagnosed children. VEEG showed higher diagnostic performance than routine EEG, and EEG frequency band power (delta, theta, alpha, beta) was correlated with cognitive impairment severity.

papers.title: Circadian disruption exacerbates alcohol-induced cardiac injury through impaired cellular quality control and increased cardiomyocyte death.
papers.summary: RNA-sequencing of hearts from alcohol-fed C57BL/6J mice at two circadian time points revealed time-of-day-dependent transcriptional programs, and circadian disruption exacerbated alcohol-induced impairment of autophagy/mitophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction, ROS production, and apoptotic cardiomyocyte death.

papers.title: Decoding user satisfaction during reading of pre-defined question-answer pairs: BCI approach using delta and gamma EEG.
papers.summary: Developed a BCI framework using 64-channel EEG to characterize implicit neural correlates of user satisfaction while reading LLM-generated question-answer pairs, with trials relabeled by post-trial Likert ratings. Satisfactory responses showed sustained frontotemporal delta enhancement during middle/late reading, dissatisfactory responses showed early right frontotemporal gamma suppression, and ShallowFBCSPNet classified very satisfied versus very dissatisfied states at 81% average accuracy under subject-mixed cross-validation.

papers.title: Cross-cohort transfer of clinical Alzheimer's EEG signatures to cognitively healthy APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 risk carriers using differentiable logic gate networks.
papers.summary: Differentiable logic gate networks trained on EEG power spectral density from a clinical Alzheimer's disease cohort were transferred without retraining to cognitively healthy APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 risk carriers, yielding higher exploratory AD-like EEG signature scores in dual carriers, though the association did not survive Holm correction.

papers.title: Circadian Misalignment and Chrononutrition in Type 2 Diabetes: Mechanistic Insights and Translational Gaps.
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates molecular, clinical, nutritional, and pharmacological evidence linking circadian misalignment to type 2 diabetes, emphasizing chrononutrition, time-restricted eating, melatonin/MTNR1B, continuous glucose monitoring, and chronopharmacology, while concluding that diabetes-specific interventional and complication-outcome evidence remains limited.

papers.title: Impact of Music as Environmental Enrichment on Chronic Stress and Anxiety-Related Responses in Broiler Chickens.
papers.journal: Animal science journal = Nihon chikusan Gakkaiho
papers.summary: Broiler chickens exposed to classical music for 6 h daily from 1 to 40 days of age had significantly lower feather corticosterone concentrations than controls, indicating reduced chronic stress, but no significant treatment effects were detected on attention bias test behavioral measures.

papers.title: Fear-EEG-AI: A Conceptual and Operational Framework for Designing EEG-AI Systems for the Inference of Fear-Compatible Neurophysiological States.
papers.summary: This paper introduces the Fear-EEG-AI Framework, a technology-independent architecture with three hierarchical levels, six cross-cutting principles, eight observable dimensions, an alignment index, and five validation evidence levels for designing and validating EEG-AI systems that infer fear-compatible neurophysiological states, applied to eight eligible studies with 67.2% exact inter-rater agreement (quadratic-weighted κ=0.741).

papers.title: CSTO-Net: Cross-View Spectral-Transport and Topology-Operator Network for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.summary: CSTO-Net integrates dynamic differential entropy node attributes with Pearson correlation and phase-locking value graphs, using cross-view spectral transport routing and a graph-operator commutator for EEG emotion recognition. It achieved 93.95% valence and 94.97% arousal accuracy on DEAP, and 93.12% on SEED, with ablations confirming both components contribute to performance.

papers.title: Association between low-carbohydrate diet scores and macrovascular events or all-cause mortality in adults with type 1 diabetes in Japan.
papers.summary: In a multicenter prospective cohort of 352 Japanese adults with type 1 diabetes, higher low-carbohydrate diet scores were associated with lower risk of macrovascular events or all-cause mortality. The Plant low-carbohydrate diet score showed the strongest inverse association (HR 0.85; 95% CI 0.76-0.94).

papers.title: Nutrition, Circadian Regulation, and the Gut-Melatonin-Visceral Adipose Tissue Axis: An Integrative Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates evidence on nutrition, circadian regulation, intestinal melatonin, gut microbiota, and visceral adipose tissue function. It proposes the Gut-Melatonin-Visceral Adipose Tissue Axis as a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework, explicitly noting that direct human evidence validating the complete pathway is lacking.

papers.title: PocketTSLM: Deploying an On-Device Soft-Prompt Time-Series Language Model for Privacy-Preserving Smartphone Reasoning
papers.summary: Presents PocketTSLM, a fully on-device smartphone deployment of the OpenTSLM SoftPrompt time-series language model that injects encoded time-series embeddings instead of tokenizing raw samples. Benchmarking showed approximately 12x fewer time-series tokens than a text-serialized baseline on the same backbone, with on-device processing of 30-s Sleep-EDF EEG and 10-s 12-lead ECG clips while avoiding health data transmission.

papers.title: Perceptions of Intra-Operative EEG Brain Monitoring During Pediatric Anesthesia Among Children and Parents: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Survey.
papers.summary: An exploratory cross-sectional survey of 400 pediatric patients and parents found that 83.5% rated intra-operative EEG monitoring as important and 93% felt more reassured by it, with most willing to pay despite cost concerns. Children worried most about intraoperative awareness, while parents worried about anesthetic side effects; higher parental education and prior anesthetic exposure increased reassurance.

papers.title: Folic Acid Oversupplementation Alters Global DNA Methylation and Circadian Clock Gene Expression in FaDu Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma Cells: An Exploratory Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory in vitro study treated FaDu head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cells with folic acid and assessed viability, global DNA methylation, and circadian clock gene expression. Folic acid reduced cell viability, modestly reduced global DNA methylation at 80 μM, and significantly increased BMAL1 and PER2 mRNA without qualitative promoter methylation changes in the analyzed CpG regions.

papers.title: Balancing Local and Global Dependencies in EEG Emotion Recognition via Multi-Scale Hybrid Attention.
papers.summary: The paper proposes DSFConformer, an EEG emotion recognition framework combining multi-scale spatiotemporal convolution, Dynamic Sparse Feature Fusion, and a lightweight Transformer. On the SEED dataset, it achieved 96.08% accuracy under chronological block-wise segment-level cross-validation and 78.81% under a stricter trial-wise protocol, with ablation analyses indicating multi-scale convolution and DSFF drove performance gains while the Lite Transformer mainly improved efficiency.

papers.title: Dynamic within-person associations between problematic social media use and sleep quality among university students: The mediating role of nomophobia and the moderating role of trait rumination.
papers.summary: A 21-day daily diary study with 228 Chinese university students used dynamic structural equation modeling to test whether nomophobia mediates the daily link between problematic social media use (PSMU) and poor sleep quality, with trait rumination moderating the indirect effect. At the within-person level, increases in PSMU prospectively predicted greater nomophobia, which in turn predicted poorer sleep quality, and this indirect association was stronger in students with higher trait rumination.

papers.title: Cross-species multi-omics integration reveals lung alterations in acute kidney injury across mouse, pig, and human airway organoid models
papers.summary: Integrating Epic Cosmos clinical data with cross-species multi-omics (pig and mouse AKI models and human lung organoids), this study characterized lung alterations after acute kidney injury (AKI). The AKI-lung subgroup had higher mortality (36.67% vs. 25.45%) and longer hospital stay; mechanistically, hyper-acute pig lungs showed post-translational responses including ciliary breakdown and PDHA1 depletion, mouse lungs showed transcriptional inflammatory and PI3K/Akt activation, and human donor lungs with clinical AKI showed selective downregulation of the circadian regulator CLOCK.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
